header: "FIND A FARE": I list the trains that go from Durgapur (or from Asansol, on the Asansol tab) to a station the user picks, with the saved fare of each class. I build it from the saved fares to every stop (public.train_fare_leg) joined with the kept timetable (the departure at Durgapur, the days, the kind of train). This file is pure: the rows, the timetable and the clock are handed in. Nothing here asks RailRadar, because the fares were collected while the paid month lasted.

symbols.name: StopsAnswer
doc: The stations that have a saved fare to them, used by the search box.

members.name: label
doc: One of "Express", "Superfast", "Vande Bharat", "Shatabdi", "MEMU (local)"...; I leave it empty when the timetable is not at hand.

members.name: departure
doc: The departure at the starting station (Durgapur, or Asansol); I set null when the timetable is not at hand.

members.name: endsAt
doc: Where the train's run ends: the name RailRadar gives it, and the code.

members.name: hint
doc: True when the fares are hints from the railway's fare table (a local train).

members.name: receivedAt
doc: The OLDEST fare among the trains shown, so none is older than this.

members.name: frozen
doc: True when the paid month is over: nothing is refreshed any more.

symbols.name: cheapest
doc: The cheapest fare of a train to the stop (its lowest class), used for sorting; I return Infinity when it has none.

symbols.name: trainsOf
symbols.sig: export function trainsOf(t: Railway | AsansolTrains | null): Train[]
doc: I return every train of a timetable, whichever of the two shapes it has: Durgapur's (in groups by direction) or Asansol's (two lists).

symbols.name: buildFind
symbols.sig: export function buildFind(stop: { code: string; name: string }, rows: StopTrainRow[], railway: Railway | AsansolTrains | null, coverage: Coverage, now: DateTime, until?: string): FindAnswer | null
doc: I build the trains to a station from the saved fares and the timetable (null when the timetable could not be read); the result is null when no train has a saved fare to it.

behaviours: the trains to a station come in the order they are at Durgapur (the departure, else the arrival), joined with the timetable: names, class words, kinds, days, where each run ends
a local train's fare is flagged a hint, the others are not
the stop, the coverage and the DATE OF THE OLDEST fare (12 Nov) are carried; the paid month is open, so not frozen
after the paid month the answer is frozen
with no timetable the trains still show with the names saved with their fares, without times, in number order
a station nobody has a saved fare to has no answer
the cheapest fare of a train is its lowest class; a train with none sorts last (Infinity)
trainsOf reads both shapes of timetable: Durgapur's groups (24 trains of the sample) and Asansol's two lists (11), and nothing for none

over Asansol's timetable the trains are joined with their times AT ASANSOL, in order: 13287 (00:15), 12302 (07:20), the MEMU 63541 (04:45) among them by its time; classes, kinds and where each run ends are carried
